name: Galaris operating knowledge fr v2
description: Entirely synthetic native Goal management, Memory, Task and Document decisions. Real public tool schemas; effect-free receipts. References are never supplied to candidates.

tool_catalog.name: dataset_query
tool_catalog.description: Query one accessible data:// UUID without downloading its complete JSON. Use RFC 6901 JSON pointers, empty for root; an array at query.path becomes rows. Filter with AND, project fields, sort, paginate and aggregate all matching rows. Use expected_revision from discovery to reject changed data. Numeric aggregates return decimal strings with missing/null counts; incompatible numeric types are errors. No expressions, SQL, inferred unit conversion or date parsing. ISO date strings can be ordered only when they share the same format and timezone. Read-only; does not grant access.

tool_catalog.name: document_share
tool_catalog.description: Share an owned HTML Document with exactly one agent_id, user_id or team_id. Access read/edit grants access; none revokes only that direct grant. First call document_sharing for recipient IDs and expected_lock_version. Linking a Document never grants access.

tool_catalog.name: document_sharing
tool_catalog.description: Inspect an owned Document's grants, recipient options and lock_version. Pass its document:// URI or UUID. Use the returned recipient IDs and lock_version with document_share. Paginate options with offset/limit (50 by default, maximum 500).

tool_catalog.name: file_create
tool_catalog.description:
Create a new complete text or binary file and return its canonical URI. Use path='file://' plus name for an independent private managed file; its returned file://UUID is stable and does not expose a host path. For path providers, pass an exact file path or a collection path plus name. Use path='document://' to let Galaris assign a new document URI. Use path='data://' for an independent Dataset with valid UTF-8 JSON; its canonical URI is data://UUID and its content remains free JSON. Dataset creation requires the content argument containing complete valid JSON, for example '[]' or '{}'; omitting content is rejected before creation. Document types are text (HTML) and data (JSON); document_format remains immutable. The data option at document:// returns data://; html/dataset remain compatibility spellings. For an HTML document, content must be an editorial HTML fragment with encoding='utf-8', for example '

Report

Findings.

', not Markdown or a full HTML page with html/head/body tags. Documents accept ordinary form, style and script elements, rendered in an isolated sandbox alongside editable prose. No special app manifest is required. An HTML form declares a Dataset with data-dataset='data://UUID' (verified legacy document:// aliases also work), optionally data-dataset-alias='entries'. Inside the sandbox use galaris.datasets.read/append/replace, with the read revision for mutations; share both the page and Dataset explicitly. Source editing preserves this ordinary HTML. Use document:///attachments/ plus name to attach a file to an editable document. Choose a destination scheme returned by file_schemes; console:// is the local filesystem whenever it is advertised. With personal Skills management, create your own skill at galaris://skill/personnal///SKILL.md with valid UTF-8 Markdown starting with YAML frontmatter name: and description. File Sharing delegates to Skills validation and live permissions; a new personal package is enabled for its owner only. This private creation needs no pre-existing exact URI grant. Generic creation below galaris://skill// requires global Skills management and a sourced Task target. For galaris://processes/runs//attachments/ plus name, a sourced grant for that exact run or its attachments collection is required, along with live Process write access. Goal, Task and Process definition snapshots remain read-only: use goal_create, task_run or process_create for those business operations. Existing resources are never overwritten.

tool_catalog.name: file_edit
tool_catalog.description: Replace a 1-based inclusive range in an existing UTF-8 resource. For HTML documents, start_line/end_line identify complete blocks returned by file_read, content is valid HTML, and expected_revision is mandatory. Use this for focused prose corrections or consolidation. Match the first and last replacement blocks to that numbered range. A heading outside the range is retained: do not repeat it in content. Check the replacement with its retained neighbours before editing. Preserve useful detail and sources; Galaris document-content changes retain prior revisions. data:// Datasets use actual lines and require expected_revision; the complete result must remain valid JSON. For example start_line=10 and end_line=14 rewrites lines 10 through 14. Binary resources are rejected. Pass expected_revision for document:// or galaris://skill/ when one is already known. For Nextcloud, pass expected_etag from file_read when known; concurrent edits are rejected. Contact JSON at galaris://contact/<uuid> requires expected_etag from file_read/file_info; only display_name and coordinates are editable, and the result must remain valid JSON.

tool_catalog.name: file_read
tool_catalog.description: Read any resource URI. UTF-8 text is returned in bounded pages; small binary files are returned completely as base64. Keep large binaries out of model context: pass their exact URI to file_search with mode='semantic' for cited document passages, or use a specialized tool, or copy to console:// only when console software must handle them. Raw base64 is not decoded text or verified page coverage: do not claim full PDF/Office reading from a binary payload. Use document_analyze for exhaustive or visual analysis of documents. Use next_offset to continue text reads. Dataset JSON pages retain character offsets and include one-based start_line/end_line, total_lines and start_line_complete/end_line_complete flags for file_edit; a false flag means the first/last line is partial, so read its missing text before replacing that line. A document://folders/<uuid>/ read returns a complete JSON hierarchy page of up to 200 items, including subfolders and nested Documents, filtered by live access rights. Its fixed item budget replaces max_chars: offset and next_offset count items (offset_unit=item). Follow all pages; continuations attach to parent_key from earlier pages, and keys distinguish repeated placements. HTML Memory/document pages contain complete numbered blocks, format, profile and revision. Their offsets count blocks, not characters. A large indivisible block reports its required max_chars (up to 2 MB); the default budget stays 20,000.

tool_catalog.name: file_search
tool_catalog.description: Search a collection, or query an exact document file URI. Returns canonical resource URIs that can be passed directly to every compatible file tool. mode='semantic' on an exact PDF, Office or text file URI (including file://UUID and document attachments) for bounded RAG passages with physical pages and character offsets. Use mode='text' for lexical passages without embedding calls. Repeat with another query to investigate further; one exact-file result contains selected passages, has no pagination, and does not create a memory. Access is rechecked for each query. For exact-file RAG, index_coverage describes retrieval; indexing_status refers to the separate file catalogue. Use galaris:// to find tasks, conversation rounds, goals, goal cycles, and assigned processes; authorized skill files are searched below galaris://skill/. galaris:// supports name and text search, not semantic search; use memory:// for semantic recall. On document://, mode='name' matches titles and filenames only and returns compact metadata without body excerpts; use mode='text' or 'semantic' to search document content. memory:// retains hybrid recall in every mode. During Process input collection, identical searches can replay for 30 seconds within the same human message. Use refresh=true after a known source change; change the query or ask the human instead of repeating empty searches. On data://, text searches JSON keys and values; semantic uses the configured vector index with explicit lexical fallback. Dataset passages include JSON pointers and revisions. Use dataset_query for exact filters, projections and numeric aggregates.

tool_catalog.name: goal_complete
tool_catalog.description: Mark a Goal completed and stop future cycles, using the revision read from galaris://goal/<uuid>.

tool_catalog.name: goal_create
tool_catalog.description: Assign a new long-running Goal to an agent. The owner agent performs the work and the selected Messenger contact supervises it as its human contact. The description must be a rich-text HTML fragment; title stays plain text. The first cycle is scheduled immediately when active is true. An enabled schedule adds a Goal-specific restriction inside the global Goal time window.

items.description: One local-time weekly window, optionally shared by several weekdays.

tool_catalog.name: goal_delete
tool_catalog.description: Soft-delete a Goal. A Goal with an unfinished execution cycle cannot be deleted; complete or wait for it first.

tool_catalog.name: goal_pause
tool_catalog.description: Pause a Goal using the revision read from galaris://goal/<uuid>.

tool_catalog.name: goal_resume
tool_catalog.description: Resume a paused or errored Goal, or restart a completed Goal while preserving its history, using the revision read from galaris://goal/<uuid>.

tool_catalog.name: goal_run_now
tool_catalog.description: Schedule a Goal cycle immediately, using the revision read from galaris://goal/<uuid>. This also reactivates a paused or errored Goal when its referrer is available. By default only the current agent's Goals can be launched; the Goal connection's management scope permits the delegated agents' Goals.

tool_catalog.name: goal_update
tool_catalog.description: Update a Goal using the revision read from galaris://goal/<uuid>. Any omitted field is preserved. description must be a rich-text HTML fragment; title stays plain text. The owner assignment can only change before the first cycle; a supplied referrer is always a human Galaris user. An enabled schedule can only further restrict the global Goal time window.

items.description: One local-time weekly window, optionally shared by several weekdays.

tool_catalog.name: goal_update_suivi
tool_catalog.description: Replace the tracking HTML of one visible Goal using the revision returned by file_read on galaris://goal/<uuid>. By default only the current agent's Goals can be updated; the Goal connection's scope permits the delegated agents' Goals.

tool_catalog.name: memory_forget
tool_catalog.description: Permanently forget one of your memories, including every stored revision. Use the exact UUID returned by file_search on memory://. Items directly representing Contacts, Documents, Files or other source-owned resources cannot be forgotten here. A personal fact linked to those resources remains forgettable.

tool_catalog.name: memory_remember
tool_catalog.description: Store one durable governed memory as one atomic structured fact. Supply fact with subject_ref (an existing Contact or Document URI; omit for the current contact or agent), one snake_case predicate and one raw scalar value or {ref: URI}. Split independent values into separate facts. Do not narrate who said it or when: attribution and timestamps are linked by the server. Legacy content accepts a structured fact encoded as JSON, never prose or HTML. Use sparingly for an explicit memory request, a correction, or an especially important confirmed fact worth retaining immediately. Leave routine extraction and duplicate checking to Dream; skip equivalent known memories. Storage is immediate and auditable. Never store contact emails, phone numbers, postal addresses or messaging identifiers here: Contacts handles them separately. Keep a person's preferences or decisions without their coordinates. For a correction or conflicting claim about a known personal memory, supply contradicts_memory_id and its expected_revision: both claims are preserved with an explicit contradiction link. A changed target requires rereading; never guess its UUID. Keywords may be an array of strings or a JSON-encoded array string. Optional temporal contains partial year/month/day/weekday (Monday=1..Sunday=7)/hour/minute in Galaris's configured timezone. Unset components are wildcards. An anchor excludes automatic recall outside its period and forces priority inclusion when it matches, subject to access and context budgets. Use it for intended reminders, not historical timestamps or ordinary facts; never default to today.

anyOf.description: Unset components are wildcards; weekday uses ISO Monday=1, Sunday=7.
One subject/predicate/value assertion; provenance and time live elsewhere.

subject_ref.description: Existing memory:// contact, document:// resource or own galaris://agent/ URI. Omit for the current contact or agent.

predicate.description: One stable snake_case property, such as preferred_language or wants.

tool_catalog.name: task_get
tool_catalog.description: Return a compact operational view of a task with its canonical resource URI, target agent, requester, objective, feedback, actionable terminal diagnostics, progress, amendment eligibility, and explicit waits such as the colleague, question, and deadline. Accept a canonical galaris://task/ URI, a full UUID, or a unique UUID prefix.

tool_catalog.name: tools_list
tool_catalog.description: List authorized MCP functions and distinguish those present in this run from those requiring a new execution context, grouped by application tool.
